newsitem.title: UK: Angerstein says in talks to buy Mumford.
newsitem.headline: Angerstein says in talks to buy Mumford.

text.p: Lloyd's of London investment vehicle Angerstein Underwriting Trust Plc said on Thursday it was in discussions with the shareholders of J E Mumford Holdings Limited which might lead to the acquisition of the company.

"We had identified Mumford as our first choice for a partner following a detailed strategic review...and we are delighted that our discussions with John Mumford and his team are coming to fruition," Angerstein chairman-designate John Kennedy said in a statement.

Mumford is the holding company of J E Mumford (Underwriting Agencies) Limited, the managing agency for Lloyd's insurance syndicate 1141, which has 76.1 million stg underwriting capacity for 1996 and has been profitable since it began in 1989, the statement added.
Angerstein is one of the original dozen corporate investors set up in 1993 when Lloyd's changed its rules to allow in limited liability corporate capital from 1994.

Angerstein said in its 1996 annual report that it was "pursuing ways in which it might ensure access to attractive underwriting positions, in return for providing underwriters with a more secure capital base."
Originally, Angerstein was set up to invest in a spread of Lloyd's 160 plus insurance syndicates.
Syndicate 1141 concentrates on reinsurance business and "is a recognised leader of specialist U.S. casualty reinsurance, particularly professional indemnity business," the statement said.
